title: The Most Coverage Months One Rider Premium Charge May Carry
content:
Every rider premium charge raised on one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders is bounded by a ceiling on the coverage months it may carry, and the ceiling follows from the rider's standing.

## The rule

1. Where the rider stands at active and the rider record carries no day it ended, the most one charge may carry is a benefit year's worth of twelve coverage months.
2. Where the rider stands suspended for unpaid premium, the most one charge may carry is the coverage months the days of grace the rider held allows cover, reckoned in whole months at thirty days to the month, any part month being dropped.
3. Otherwise, the most one charge may carry is the whole calendar months from the day benefits became payable to the handling date.

## The second case by rider

| Rider | Days of grace allowed | Coverage months they cover |
|---|---|---|
| Ridgecrest Preventive Dental Rider | 60 | 2 |
| Ridgecrest Vision Plus Rider | 60 | 2 |
| Ridgecrest Hearing Advantage Rider | 60 | 2 |
| Ridgecrest Comprehensive Dental Rider | 60 | 2 |
| Ridgecrest Premier Dental Rider | 90 | 3 |
| Ridgecrest Dental Vision Hearing Bundle Rider | 90 | 3 |

## Condition and ceiling

| The rider's standing | The ceiling |
|---|---|
| Active, the record carrying no day it ended | 12 coverage months |
| Suspended for unpaid premium | 2 coverage months on a rider allowing 60 days of grace; 3 on a rider allowing 90 |
| Any other standing | The whole calendar months from the day benefits became payable to the handling date |

In every case the ceiling is never fewer than none.

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

- A rider standing at active with no day it ended: the ceiling is 12, however many months have passed since benefits became payable.
- A rider allowing 90 days of grace and standing suspended for unpaid premium: the ceiling is 3.
- A rider in its waiting period, benefits having become payable 5 whole calendar months before the handling date: the ceiling is 5.
